instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've held my number up like you. That gets us called next. Do you want the part enough to walk through that door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking which number I had. They haven't called us. I don't want them laughing at me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, numbers checked. I can walk you in or take you home. Which are we doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Will you risk it with me there, or shall I get the car?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my napkin over the plate like you. Dinner finished; honest talk now. Do you want the truth about renewing our lease?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was keeping a fly off. Yes, the truth, but nothing that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your plate covered, then. I can give you my honest answer or a peaceful dinner. Which?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Answer, but begin with 'we're fine'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That gives me your first sentence. Do you want to hear mine, even if it's different?

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've closed the flight page like you. That's our flight chosen. I still haven't bought the anniversary tickets; can you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I closed a duplicate tab. We haven't chosen a flight. I thought you just needed help choosing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, one page at a time. I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I find the words?

beats.text: I've pulled a chair out like you. Seats saved. I wasn't just late to the reunion; can I tell you?

beats.text: I moved that chair so people could get past. At the reunion I did save you one. Was it traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd enjoy yourself more without me. Will you sit beside me now?

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pressed zero on my calculator like you. Accounts finished. You can stop the cheerful shopkeeper voice now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Zero was our takings. Someone has to keep morale up; you're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, clear figures. I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom, then practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay out here with me. You don't have to go behind a door to be upset once we've closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I left my television on like you. A proper welcome for visitors. Have you got company tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. I leave it on because I hate coming back to silence. I pretend someone else is there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, ready for company. Could you ask me over instead of telling me you're managing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Invite me without that promise. I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed the fair route off like you. Sensible precautions. Now let's tell the stallholders they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed off a flooded shortcut. You panicked and told them the whole fair was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, transport precautions. I'll tell everyone the main arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two people cancelled their vans because you told them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Call it a transport hiccup in the update; they need a calm message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed off the treasurer's name like you. Problem dealt with. Let's tell everyone they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cross off people I've called. The money was in the bank bag; you had me tell everyone the treasurer stole it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, completed calls. I'll reassure them now that it's all accounted for. Could you introduce the update?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole committee heard you crying about theft on the call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll call them together. Introduce it as a routine balance update, and I'll give them the total.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stirred sugar into my tea like you. Ready to open the scholarship letter, once we find clean teaspoons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't add sugar; I was stirring to cool mine. Here's a clean spoon. Open the letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, cooling it first. I'll need another cup now; this one's sweet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you scared of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap, we'll need to mark which has sugar. Have you got a pen that writes on mugs?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my train ticket like yours. Ready for the barrier. Before we discuss me moving out, check the departure time again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's a receipt folded to fit my wallet. Your train's six twelve; we've checked it five times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, keep it safe. Does my ticket need unfolding at the barrier?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you're coming onto the platform, do you need a ticket too? Let's check that before we go.
